lyrics:
[Intro: soft electric guitar chords, bass, birds and a distant bus]

[Verse 1: warm, relaxed, behind the beat]
Got a bench on the corner by the hardware store
Been here since the paper, I'll be here some more
The buses come in and the buses go
I don't need to be on one, far as I know

[Chorus: horns enter softly, voice lifts a little]
I've got a bench with a view of nothing
Watching the day go by
A bench with a view of nothing much
And nothing's doing fine

[Verse 2: warm, a little rueful]
I left a job with my name on the glass
Thirty years of hurry and it all went past
Had a watch that told me where to be
Gave it to my grandson, now it's telling me

[Chorus: horns, voice lifts a little]
I've got a bench with a view of nothing
Watching the day go by
A bench with a view of nothing much
And nothing's doing fine

[Bridge: drums push, voice stronger]
Folks walk by and they ask if I'm alright
I say I've never been so on time
There's a pigeon here who knows my name
And every afternoon's the same

[Final Chorus: full band, relaxed]
I've got a bench with a view of nothing
Watching the day go by
A bench with a view of nothing much
And nothing's doing fine

[Outro: whistled melody over guitar and bass, street sounds, fade]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 104 BPM, 4/4, G major. A slow, rolling, unhurried soul groove. Easy and settled.

VOICE: Male, warm, weathered and a little hoarse, a Southern soul voice that sings just behind the beat and never forces a note. A slightly stronger push in the bridge. He whistles the tune through the outro.

INSTRUMENTS: A clean electric guitar playing soft chords and small sliding fills. A round, simple bass. A relaxed drum kit with a light snare. A horn section playing long, quiet notes. Acoustic guitar strumming. Street sounds: birds, a bus pulling away.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar, bass and street sounds. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:36 Chorus 1, horns. 0:56 Verse 2. 1:20 Chorus 2. 1:40 Bridge. 2:00 Final chorus. 2:20 Outro, the whistled tune over guitar and bass with street sounds, fading by 2:42.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1960s Memphis soul: dry, warm and spare, a small band in a room, the voice close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The whistling in the outro at 2:20.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original narrator is young, far from home and going nowhere. This one is old, at home and finished with going anywhere. He gave his watch to his grandson. The stillness is a reward.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Ease, a backward glance, contentment.
